subtype: Approach: presenting an unexpected result honestly [Revision]
passage: Sit, beta. Your grandmother Reena has a story about a bean plant. When I was ten, we grew beans for the school fair. I put one pot in the dark cupboard and wrote on my paper that it would stay green. It grew, but pale as chalk. My classmate Ganga whispered, "Change it, write green." I nearly did. Then I thought, the plant did not lie, so why should I? At the fair I stood by my board and said, "I guessed green, and it turned pale, and that surprised me." The old teacher judging asked why. I said I did not know yet. He gave me a ribbon, but I remember his smile more.

qa.q: What colour was the plant that grew in the cupboard?
What was Reena feeling when Ganga whispered to change the paper?
qa.a: She felt tempted and uneasy, since she nearly did it and then reasoned that the plant had not lied.

qa.q: What choice did young Reena make at the fair, and why did it work out?
qa.a: She chose to show the pale plant and say she was surprised, and the judge valued her honesty enough to give her a ribbon.

qa.q: How did the judging teacher see Reena's answer that she did not know yet?
qa.a: The teacher seems to have taken it as honest work, giving her a ribbon and a smile.

grounding: A child keeps her unexpected pale-plant result and explains her surprise instead of changing the results.
